author: BBC News
description:
Andy Burnham has announced that he is seeking permission to stand in the upcoming Gorton and Denton parliamentary MP by-election.

Currently mayor of Greater Manchester, he insisted he wants to back the UK's Labour government "not undermine it" and said that the decision to announce his intentions had been "difficult".

The seat in Greater Manchester is vacant after Labour's Andrew Gwynne stood down on Friday as MP on health grounds.

author: BBC News
description:
Russia launched drone and missile attacks on Ukraine overnight, killing one person and injuring 23 others despite taking part in talks with the US aimed at ending the war.
 
The mayor of Ukrainian capital Kyiv said one person had died and four had been wounded following a "massive enemy attack", while Kharkiv's mayor reported that 19 people had been hurt during a sustained assault on the city.
 
Delegations from Russia, Ukraine and the US have been meeting in Abu Dhabi in the first trilateral talks since the Kremlin launched a full-scale invasion of its neighbour in 2022.
 
A source has told the BBC that some progress had been made but the key issue of territory remains unresolved.

author: BBC News
description:
The White House has made its first comments since US President Donald Trump sparked a row by saying that NATO troops had stayed “a little back” off the front lines during the war in Afghanistan.
 
UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said the words were "insulting and frankly appalling”.
 
Prince Harry, who served in Afghanistan, has called for the sacrifices of Nato soldiers to be "spoken about truthfully and with respect".
 
The White House's deputy press secretary said that Trump was right to have stressed that America's contribution to NATO dwarf those of other countries. There was no direct response to the outrage caused.
